question: Which implications in Research 0168 fail, and can quotient descent, role cycling and a genuine interval period-three witness be checked separately?
level: External exact finite maps and one polynomial certificate; no native semantics or catalog growth.

corrected_source.binding: Historical bytes are identified by base_commit; the live note is corrected and is not executable input.

imported_assumptions: Li and Yorke, Period Three Implies Chaos (1975), Theorem 1, https://www.its.caltech.edu/~matilde/LiYorke.pdf: a continuous self-map of a real interval with b=F(a), c=F^2(a), d=F^3(a) and d<=a<b<c (or reversed inequalities) has points of every least period and the stated uncountable set. The theorem is not reproved or executed.

Elementary real ordered-field rules: a polynomial is continuous; powers of a nonnegative real are nonnegative; a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients and positive constant is positive on [0,1]. These justify the symbolic zero exclusion, not a finite sample extrapolation.

For a surjective map q on finite sets, g with qF=gq exists iff qF is constant on every q-fibre. Sufficiency is checked by constructing g and checking every state; failure retains a conflicting pair. No native quotient authorization follows.
interface: Finite state ordinals denote only experiment-local set elements. A phase label, a full-cycle return map, an observed quotient and an interval map remain different objects. No mapping from Adva identities to these examples is claimed.

fixtures.square_map: f(x)=x^2 on [-1,1]. Check polynomial composition f^3=x^8 and factor f^3-x=x(x-1)(1+x+...+x^6). Nonnegative factor certificate excludes roots in (0,1); for x<0, x^8-x>0. Roots 0,1 are fixed. Collision -1/2,1/2 witnesses non-injectivity.
fixtures.tent_map: T(x)=2x on [0,1/2], 2-2x on [1/2,1]. Check continuity at the join, endpoint self-map bounds, orbit 2/7 -> 4/7 -> 6/7 -> 2/7, distinctness and the printed Li-Yorke inequality. Only this fixed analytic template supplies the interval hypothesis.
fixtures.role_cycle: Six tagged states (phase,value), phase in {0,1,2}, value in {0,1}. S increments phase. Its exact period is 3, its phase-zero return S^3 is identity, and forgetting phase yields identity. FiniteSet is not RealInterval.
fixtures.history_lift: Base F(0)=F(1)=0. Enumerate its valid histories of lengths 1..5; append the next value, check projection commutation and prefix recovery for every image. Retain a singleton with no predecessor under append. Injectivity on these histories is distinct from surjectivity on all nonempty histories.
fixtures.controls: Identity has F^3(x)=x but no least-period-three point; a fixed tent point fails strict orbit inequalities; role-tag and finite-quotient cycles are explicitly refused as interval-theorem witnesses; one perturbed polynomial factor fails the coefficient identity.
